Country Bread

Served at: Feast of the Ass

One 9-inch (23 cm) loafPrep 15 minCook 1 hr 30 min

Country Bread is a rustic, hearty loaf traditionally baked and enjoyed during the Feast of the Ass, a medieval festival celebrating the biblical story of the Flight into Egypt. This bread symbolizes sustenance and humility, reflecting the simple, nourishing food of the time and adding a warm, communal element to the celebration.

Ingredients

  • 3 cups (360 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1 cup (120 g) whole wheat flour
  • 1 1/4 cups (300 ml) warm water
  • 2 1/4 tsp (1 packet) active dry yeast
  • 1 1/2 tsp salt
  • 1 tbsp (15 ml) olive oil
  • 1 tbsp (12 g) honey or molasses

Method

  1. In a small bowl, dissolve the yeast in warm water and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour, whole wheat flour, and salt.
  3. Add the yeast mixture, olive oil, and honey or molasses to the flour mixture.
  4. Stir until a shaggy dough forms, then turn it out onto a floured surface and knead for about 8-10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
  5. Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with a clean cloth, and let it rise in a warm place for about 1 hour or until doubled in size.
  6. Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C).
  7. Punch down the dough and shape it into a round loaf.
  8. Place the loaf on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper or a lightly floured baking stone.
  9. Optionally, score the top of the loaf with a sharp knife to allow for expansion.
  10. Bake for 30-35 minutes until the crust is golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
  11. Remove from the oven and let cool on a wire rack before slicing.

Tips

  • For a more rustic texture, substitute half of the all-purpose flour with rye flour.
  • Add a handful of seeds like sunflower or flaxseed to the dough for extra flavor and nutrition.
  • Use a Dutch oven to bake the bread for a crispier crust by preheating it in the oven and baking the loaf inside with the lid on for the first 20 minutes.
